desc:
A frog sits on the first stone of a row; heights[i] is the height of stone i. In one jump the frog may move forward by any distance from 1 to k stones, i.e. from index i to any j with i < j ≤ i + k that exists. A jump from stone i to stone j costs |heights[i] - heights[j]| energy.

Return the minimum total energy to reach the last stone (0 if there is only one stone).

Example: heights = [10, 30, 40, 50, 20], k = 3 gives 30 via 10 → 30 → 20.
hints: With k = 2 the answer needs only the previous two states. What changes for larger k?
Let best(i) be the least energy to reach stone i. The previous stone of the optimal route is some j in [i - k, i - 1].
best(i) = min over j in [max(0, i-k), i-1] of best(j) + |h[i] - h[j]|, with best(0) = 0. Loop over at most k candidates for each i.
editorial: The last jump into stone i starts at some stone j with i - k ≤ j ≤ i - 1, and the route up to j must be optimal for j. Therefore best(i) = min(best(j) + |h[i] - h[j]|) over those j, and best(0) = 0. The answer is best(n-1).

Each of the n states examines at most k predecessors: O(n · k) time and O(n) space (the full table is kept because any of the last k values may be needed). The absolute difference depends on both ends of the jump, so unlike plain 'sum of the previous k' recurrences it cannot be sped up with a running window; for these constraints n · k ≤ 500,000 operations.
